title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 18. Beholding Sri Gopinatha after the Journey through Gauda
html:
At Ramakeli the Lord blesses Sanatana and his brother; He turns back from Natyashala, stays with Advaita, meets His mother and the devotees of Navadvipa, and returns to Puri, where with Nityananda and Gadadhara He honours the prasada of Gopinatha

Verse 1

ततो भक्तैर्वृतः कृष्णो रामकेलिं जगाम ह।
श्रुत्वा तत्रागमद्द्रष्टुं प्रभुपादं सनातनः॥१॥

tato bhaktairvṛtaḥ kṛṣṇo rāmakeliṁ jagāma ha|
śrutvā tatrāgamaddraṣṭuṁ prabhupādaṁ sanātanaḥ||1||

tatah — then; bhaktaih — by devotees; vritah — surrounded; krishnah — Krishna; ramakelim — to Ramakeli; jagama — went; ha — indeed; shrutva — hearing; tatra — there; agamat — came; drashtum — to see; prabhu-padam — the Lord's feet; sanatanah — Sanatana.

1Then Krishna, surrounded by His devotees, came to Ramakeli1. Hearing of this, Sanatana came there to see the Lord's feet.

Verse 2

प्रभुं दृष्ट्वा प्रीतमनाः प्रपतन्धरणीतले।
दशनाग्रे तृणं धृत्वा सानुजः प्राह केशवम्॥२॥

prabhuṁ dṛṣṭvā prītamanāḥ prapatandharaṇītale|
daśanāgre tṛṇaṁ dhṛtvā sānujaḥ prāha keśavam||2||

prabhum — the Lord; drishtva — seeing; prita-manah — glad at heart; prapatan — falling; dharani-tale — to the ground; dashana-agre — between his teeth; trinam — a straw; dhritva — holding; sa-anujah — with his younger brother; praha — said; keshavam — to Keshava.

2Seeing the Lord, he rejoiced at heart; together with his younger brother he fell to the ground and, holding a straw between his teeth2, said to Keshava:

Verse 3

मद्विधो नास्ति पापात्मा नापराधी च कश्चन।
परिहारेऽपि लज्जा मे किं ब्रुवे पुरुषोत्तम॥३॥

madvidho nāsti pāpātmā nāparādhī ca kaścana|
parihāre'pi lajjā me kiṁ bruve puruṣottama||3||

mat-vidhah — like me; na asti — there is no; papa-atma — sinner; na — no; aparadhi — offender; cha — and; kashchana — anyone; parihare — in excusing myself; api — even; lajja — shame; me — to me; kim — what; bruve — shall I say; purushottama — O Purushottama.

3"There is no sinner like me, no such offender anywhere. I am ashamed even to excuse myself — what can I say, O Purushottama?"

Verse 4

स्वपादं तस्य शिरसि धृत्वा प्राह जनार्दनः।
वृन्दावननिवासी त्वं सत्यं सत्यं न संशयः॥४॥

svapādaṁ tasya śirasi dhṛtvā prāha janārdanaḥ|
vṛndāvananivāsī tvaṁ satyaṁ satyaṁ na saṁśayaḥ||4||

sva-padam — His foot; tasya — his; shirasi — on the head; dhritva — placing; praha — said; janardanah — Janardana; vrindavana-nivasi — a dweller of Vrindavana; tvam — you; satyam satyam — truly, truly; na — no; samshayah — doubt.

4Janardana placed His foot on his head and said, "You are a dweller of Vrindavana — truly, truly, there is no doubt.

Verse 5

मथुरां गन्तुमिच्छामि त्वया सार्धं यथासुखम्।
लुप्ततीर्थस्य प्राकट्यं तथा वृन्दावनस्य च॥५॥

mathurāṁ gantumicchāmi tvayā sārdhaṁ yathāsukham|
luptatīrthasya prākaṭyaṁ tathā vṛndāvanasya ca||5||

mathuram — to Mathura; gantum — to go; icchami — I wish; tvaya — you; sardham — together with; yatha-sukham — at ease; lupta-tirthasya — of the lost holy places; prakatyam — the manifestation; tatha — likewise; vrindavanasya — of Vrindavana; cha — and.

5I wish to go at leisure to Mathura together with you. But to reveal the lost holy places3, and Vrindavana as well —

Verse 6

कर्तुमर्हसि तत्सर्वं मत्कृपातो भविष्यति।
भक्तिस्वरूपिणी साक्षात्प्रेमभक्तिप्रदायिनी॥६॥

kartumarhasi tatsarvaṁ matkṛpāto bhaviṣyati|
bhaktisvarūpiṇī sākṣātpremabhaktipradāyinī||6||

kartum — to accomplish; arhasi — you should; tat — that; sarvam — all; mat-kripatah — by My mercy; bhavishyati — it will come about; bhakti-svarupini — devotion itself embodied; sakshat — directly; prema-bhakti-pradayini — bestowing loving devotion.

6that is your task: all of it will come about by My mercy — for My mercy is devotion itself embodied, and it bestows loving devotion."

Verse 7

श्रुत्वा प्राह महाबुद्धिः सानुजः श्रीसनातनः।
आरामः कृष्णचन्द्रस्य रम्यं वृन्दावनं शुभम्॥७॥

śrutvā prāha mahābuddhiḥ sānujaḥ śrīsanātanaḥ|
ārāmaḥ kṛṣṇacandrasya ramyaṁ vṛndāvanaṁ śubham||7||

shrutva — hearing; praha — said; maha-buddhih — the most wise; sa-anujah — with his younger brother; shri-sanatanah — Sri Sanatana; aramah — the pleasure-garden; krishna-chandrasya — of Krishnachandra; ramyam — lovely; vrindavanam — Vrindavana; shubham — auspicious.

7Hearing this, the most wise Sri Sanatana, with his younger brother, said, "Vrindavana is the pleasure-garden of Krishnachandra, lovely and auspicious:

Verse 8

श्रीराधया सह कृष्णो यत्र क्रीडति सर्वदा।
अगम्यं योगिभिर्नित्यं देवसिद्धैर्नरेतरैः॥८॥

śrīrādhayā saha kṛṣṇo yatra krīḍati sarvadā|
agamyaṁ yogibhirnityaṁ devasiddhairnaretaraiḥ||8||

shri-radhaya saha — with Sri Radha; krishnah — Krishna; yatra — where; kridati — plays; sarvada — always; agamyam — inaccessible; yogibhih — to yogis; nityam — ever; deva-siddhaih — to gods and siddhas; nara-itaraih — to men and other beings.

8there Krishna plays for ever with Sri Radha; it is for ever beyond the reach of yogis, of gods and siddhas, of men and of other beings.

Verse 9

निर्जनं तज्जनाद्यैश्च गत्वा किं स्यात्सुखाय च।
त्वत्कृपाशस्त्ररूपेण छित्त्वा मे दृढशृङ्खलाम्॥९॥

nirjanaṁ tajjanādyaiśca gatvā kiṁ syātsukhāya ca|
tvatkṛpāśastrarūpeṇa chittvā me dṛḍhaśṛṅkhalām||9||

nirjanam — solitary; tat — that (place); jana-adyaih — with crowds of people and the like; cha — and; gatva — going; kim — what; syat — would there be; sukhaya — for happiness; cha — and; tvat-kripa-shastra-rupena — with the sword of Your mercy; chhittva — cutting; me — my; dridha-shrinkhalam — strong chain.

9It is a solitary place — what joy would there be in going there with crowds of people? With the sword of Your mercy You have cut my strong chain —

Verse 10

राजपात्रादिरूपां च प्रापय्य निजसन्निधिम्।
शक्तिसञ्चारणं कृत्वा कुरु कृष्ण यथासुखम्॥१०॥

rājapātrādirūpāṁ ca prāpayya nijasannidhim|
śaktisañcāraṇaṁ kṛtvā kuru kṛṣṇa yathāsukham||10||

raja-patra-adi-rupam — in the form of a royal ministership and the like; cha — and; prapayya — bringing (me); nija-sannidhim — into Your presence; shakti-sancharanam — the infusion of power; kritva — making; kuru — do; krishna — O Krishna; yatha-sukham — as You please.

10my royal ministership and the rest — and brought me into Your presence. So now infuse Your power into me, O Krishna, and do as You please."

Verse 11

तद्वाक्यामृतमेवं हि पीत्वा प्राह हसन्प्रभुः।
भवन्मनोरथं कृष्णः सदा पूर्णं करिष्यति॥११॥

tadvākyāmṛtamevaṁ hi pītvā prāha hasanprabhuḥ|
bhavanmanorathaṁ kṛṣṇaḥ sadā pūrṇaṁ kariṣyati||11||

tat-vakya-amritam — the nectar of his words; evam — thus; hi — indeed; pitva — drinking; praha — said; hasan — laughing; prabhuh — the Lord; bhavat-manoratham — your desire; krishnah — Krishna; sada — always; purnam — fulfilled; karishyati — will make.

11Having drunk the nectar of his words, the Lord laughed and said, "Krishna will always fulfil your desires."

Verse 12

एवं तं परिसन्तोष्य कृष्णो नाट्यस्थलं गतः।
रजन्यां चिन्तयामास सत्यमुक्तं न संशयः॥१२॥

evaṁ taṁ parisantoṣya kṛṣṇo nāṭyasthalaṁ gataḥ|
rajanyāṁ cintayāmāsa satyamuktaṁ na saṁśayaḥ||12||

evam — thus; tam — him; parisantoshya — satisfying; krishnah — Krishna; natya-sthalam — to the dancing-place; gatah — went; rajanyam — at night; chintayam asa — reflected; satyam — truly; uktam — has been said; na — no; samshayah — doubt.

12Having comforted him thus, Krishna went as far as the dancing-place4, and at night He reflected: "Truly, it was well said, there is no doubt:

Verse 13

सनातनेन कृतिना तन्मुखेन च माधवः।
मामाह निर्जनं सत्यं वृन्दारण्यं सुदुर्लभम्॥१३॥

sanātanena kṛtinā tanmukhena ca mādhavaḥ|
māmāha nirjanaṁ satyaṁ vṛndāraṇyaṁ sudurlabham||13||

sanatanena — by Sanatana; kritina — the wise; tat-mukhena — through his mouth; cha — and; madhavah — Madhava; mam — to Me; aha — said; nirjanam — solitary; satyam — truly; vrinda-aranyam — the forest of Vrinda; su-durlabham — very hard to attain.

13through the mouth of the wise Sanatana it was Madhava Himself who spoke to Me — the forest of Vrinda is indeed solitary and very hard to attain.

Verse 14

लोकसङ्घैर्गते नित्यं दुःखमेव न संशयः।
सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा गमिष्यामि दक्षिणं चाधुना व्रजे॥१४॥

lokasaṅghairgate nityaṁ duḥkhameva na saṁśayaḥ|
saṅgaṁ tyaktvā gamiṣyāmi dakṣiṇaṁ cādhunā vraje||14||

loka-sanghaih — with crowds of people; gate — when one goes; nityam — always; duhkham — misery; eva — only; na — no; samshayah — doubt; sangam — company; tyaktva — leaving; gamishyami — I shall go; dakshinam — south; cha — and; adhuna — now; vraje — I go.

14To go there with crowds of people is nothing but misery, without doubt. I shall go there leaving all company behind; and now I shall turn south."

Verse 15

एवं विचार्य भगवान्सान्द्रानन्दरसात्मकः।
प्रातरुत्थाय श्रीकृष्णो नित्यानन्दसमन्वितः॥१५॥

evaṁ vicārya bhagavānsāndrānandarasātmakaḥ|
prātarutthāya śrīkṛṣṇo nityānandasamanvitaḥ||15||

evam — thus; vicharya — considering; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sandra-ananda-rasa-atmakah — whose very self is the rasa of dense bliss; pratah — in the morning; utthaya — rising; shri-krishnah — Sri Krishna; nityananda-samanvitah — together with Nityananda.

15Having considered thus, Bhagavan Sri Krishna, whose very self is the rasa of dense bliss, rose in the morning and, together with Nityananda,

Verse 16

अद्वैताचार्यनिलयं जगाम सत्वरं मुदा।
तेन संपूजितस्तत्र स्थितो भक्तसुखप्रदः॥१६॥

advaitācāryanilayaṁ jagāma satvaraṁ mudā|
tena saṁpūjitastatra sthito bhaktasukhapradaḥ||16||

advaita-acharya-nilayam — to the abode of Advaita Acharya; jagama — went; satvaram — swiftly; muda — joyfully; tena — by him; sampujitah — honoured; tatra — there; sthitah — stayed; bhakta-sukha-pradah — the giver of happiness to the devotees.

16went joyfully and swiftly to the abode of Advaita Acharya. Honoured by him, the Giver of happiness to His devotees stayed there.

Verse 17

अच्युतेनाप्यविरतं कौतुकानन्दवर्धनः।
परिहासरसामोदी हरिदासदयापरः॥१७॥

acyutenāpyavirataṁ kautukānandavardhanaḥ|
parihāsarasāmodī haridāsadayāparaḥ||17||

achyutena — with Achyuta; api — also; aviratam — unceasingly; kautuka-ananda-vardhanah — increasing the joy of play; parihasa-rasa-amodi — delighting in the rasa of jests; haridasa-daya-parah — intent on mercy to Haridasa.

17With Achyuta5 He ceaselessly increased the joy of play, delighting in the rasa of jests, and was full of mercy towards Haridasa.

Verse 18

हरिसङ्कीर्तनं रात्रौ कुर्वन्स भक्तवेष्टितः।
ननर्त परमप्रीतो नित्यानन्दसमन्वितः॥१८॥

harisaṅkīrtanaṁ rātrau kurvansa bhaktaveṣṭitaḥ|
nanarta paramaprīto nityānandasamanvitaḥ||18||

hari-sankirtanam — the sankirtana of Hari; ratrau — at night; kurvan — performing; sah — He; bhakta-veshtitah — surrounded by devotees; nanarta — danced; parama-pritah — in supreme delight; nityananda-samanvitah — together with Nityananda.

18At night, surrounded by His devotees, He performed the sankirtana of Hari and, in supreme delight, danced together with Nityananda.

Verse 19

मातरं भक्तवृन्दं च मातृभक्तशिरोमणिः।
नवद्वीपात्समानय्य तद्दुःखं परिमोचयन्॥१९॥

mātaraṁ bhaktavṛndaṁ ca mātṛbhaktaśiromaṇiḥ|
navadvīpātsamānayya tadduḥkhaṁ parimocayan||19||

mataram — His mother; bhakta-vrindam — the devotees; cha — and; matri-bhakta-shiromanih — the crest-jewel of those devoted to their mothers; navadvipat — from Navadvipa; samanayya — having brought; tat-duhkham — their grief; parimochayan — dispelling.

19The crest-jewel of those devoted to their mothers had His mother and the devotees brought from Navadvipa and dispelled their grief;

Verse 20

तया पाचितमन्नं च चातुर्विध्यं यथोचितम्।
भक्ताह्लादशतैर्भुक्तो नित्यानन्दकुतूहली॥२०॥

tayā pācitamannaṁ ca cāturvidhyaṁ yathocitam|
bhaktāhlādaśatairbhukto nityānandakutūhalī||20||

taya — by her; pachitam — cooked; annam — food; cha — and; chaturvidhyam — of the four kinds; yatha-uchitam — as was fitting; bhakta-ahlada-shataih — amid the hundredfold delight of the devotees; bhuktah — partook; nityananda-kutuhali — playful with Nityananda.

20and the food of four kinds6 that she had duly cooked He ate amid the hundredfold delight of the devotees, sporting with Nityananda.

Verse 21

एवं श्रीभक्तवर्गाणां ग्रामे ग्रामे गृहे गृहे।
भुक्त्वा पीत्वा सुखं कृत्वा ययौ श्रीपुरुषोत्तमम्॥२१॥

evaṁ śrībhaktavargāṇāṁ grāme grāme gṛhe gṛhe|
bhuktvā pītvā sukhaṁ kṛtvā yayau śrīpuruṣottamam||21||

evam — thus; shri-bhakta-varganam — of the devotees; grame grame — in village after village; grihe grihe — in house after house; bhuktva — eating; pitva — drinking; sukham — happiness; kritva — giving; yayau — went; shri-purushottamam — to Sri Purushottama.

21Thus, eating and drinking with the devotees in village after village, in house after house, and giving them joy, He went on to Sri Purushottama.

Verse 22

श्रीमन्नित्यानन्दरामः पण्डितः श्रीगदाधरः।
गौरप्रेमसुधामत्तो गौराङ्गप्राणवल्लभः॥२२॥

śrīmannityānandarāmaḥ paṇḍitaḥ śrīgadādharaḥ|
gaurapremasudhāmatto gaurāṅgaprāṇavallabhaḥ||22||

shrimat-nityananda-ramah — glorious Nityananda-Rama; panditah — Pandita; shri-gadadharah — Sri Gadadhara; gaura-prema-sudha-mattah — intoxicated with the nectar of love for Gaura; gauranga-prana-vallabhah — dear as life to Gauranga.

22Glorious Nityananda-Rama and Sri Gadadhara Pandita, intoxicated with the nectar of love for Gaura, were dear as life to Gauranga.

Verse 23

ताभ्यामनुगतः कृष्णो गोपीनाथं ददर्श ह।
साक्षान्नन्दकुमारं च श्रीवंशीवदनं विभुम्॥२३॥

tābhyāmanugataḥ kṛṣṇo gopīnāthaṁ dadarśa ha|
sākṣānnandakumāraṁ ca śrīvaṁśīvadanaṁ vibhum||23||

tabhyam — by these two; anugatah — followed; krishnah — Krishna; gopinatham — Gopinatha; dadarsha — beheld; ha — indeed; sakshat — in person; nanda-kumaram — the son of Nanda; cha — and; shri-vamshi-vadanam — with the flute at His lips; vibhum — the all-powerful.

23Followed by these two, Krishna beheld Gopinatha7 — the son of Nanda in person, the all-powerful One, with the flute at His lips.

Verse 24

गोपीमनोरथामोदी समालिङ्ग्य स्थितो हरिः।
दृष्ट्वा गदाधरस्तत्र गौरकृष्णात्मकं सुखी॥२४॥

gopīmanorathāmodī samāliṅgya sthito hariḥ|
dṛṣṭvā gadādharastatra gaurakṛṣṇātmakaṁ sukhī||24||

gopi-manoratha-amodi — who gladdens (fulfils) the heartfelt longings of the gopis; samalingya — embracing; sthitah — stood; harih — Hari; drishtva — seeing; gadadharah — Gadadhara; tatra — there; gaura-krishna-atmakam — the one self of Gaura and Krishna; sukhi — happy.

24Hari, the delight of the gopis' heartfelt longings, embraced Him and stood still; and Gadadhara, seeing there the one self of Gaura and Krishna, was happy.

Verse 25

साक्षाद्राधास्वरूपोऽसौ तं धृत्वा निजवक्षसि।
समानीय कौतुकेन स्थापयामास निश्चलम्॥२५॥

sākṣādrādhāsvarūpo'sau taṁ dhṛtvā nijavakṣasi|
samānīya kautukena sthāpayāmāsa niścalam||25||

sakshat — in person; radha-svarupah — Radha in his own nature; asau — he; tam — Him; dhritva — holding; nija-vakshasi — to his breast; samaniya — bringing; kautukena — with eager joy; sthapayam asa — installed; nishchalam — immovably.

25He, who in his own nature is Radha Herself8, held Gopinatha to his breast, brought Him with eager joy and installed Him immovably.

Verse 26

तस्य पाचितमन्नं च गोपीनाथावशेषितम्।
गदाधृग्गौरचन्द्रस्य समीपे पुलकावृतः॥२६॥

tasya pācitamannaṁ ca gopīnāthāvaśeṣitam|
gadādhṛggauracandrasya samīpe pulakāvṛtaḥ||26||

tasya — by him; pachitam — cooked; annam — food; cha — and; gopinatha-avasheshitam — the remnants of Gopinatha; gadadhrik — Gadadhara; gaurachandrasya — of Gaurachandra; samipe — before; pulaka-avritah — thrilling all over.

26The food he himself had cooked — the remnants of Gopinatha — Gadadhara, thrilling all over, set before Gaurachandra;

Verse 27

तेनानुमोदितो हर्षात्सत्रत्रयसमन्वितम्।
प्रसादं गोपीनाथस्य विभज्य बुभुजे पुरा॥२७॥

tenānumodito harṣātsatratrayasamanvitam|
prasādaṁ gopīnāthasya vibhajya bubhuje purā||27||

tena — by him; anumoditah — urged; harshat — joyfully; satra-traya-samanvitam — in three portions; prasadam — the prasada; gopinathasya — of Gopinatha; vibhajya — dividing; bubhuje — ate; pura — first.

27and at his urging the Lord joyfully divided Gopinatha's prasada into three portions and ate first9.

Verse 28

भोजयित्वा स्वहस्तेन नित्यानन्दाय च पुनः।
गदाधरः स्वयं चापि बुभुजे रसकौतुकी॥२८॥

bhojayitvā svahastena nityānandāya ca punaḥ|
gadādharaḥ svayaṁ cāpi bubhuje rasakautukī||28||

bhojayitva — feeding; sva-hastena — with his own hand; nityanandaya — Nityananda; cha — and; punah — then; gadadharah — Gadadhara; svayam — himself; cha api — also; bubhuje — ate; rasa-kautuki — rapt in rasa.

28And Gadadhara, rapt in rasa, first fed Nityananda with his own hand, and then ate himself.

Verse 29

ततश्च गौराङ्गः सुखोपविष्टो
गदाधरेणापि स्वयं रसज्ञः।
रासोत्सुको रामरसेन मत्तो
रामोपरामे रसरामरामे॥२९॥

tataśca gaurāṅgaḥ sukhopaviṣṭo
gadādhareṇāpi svayaṁ rasajñaḥ|
rāsotsuko rāmarasena matto
rāmoparāme rasarāmarāme||29||

tatah — then; cha — and; gaurangah — Gauranga; sukha-upavishtah — seated at ease; gadadharena — with Gadadhara; api — indeed; svayam — Himself; rasa-jnah — the knower of rasa; rasa-utsukah — longing for the rasa dance; rama-rasena — with the rasa of delight; mattah — intoxicated; rama-uparame — when Rama had retired to rest; rasa-rama-rame — (rejoicing) in Him who is the delight of the delights of rasa.

29And afterwards Gauranga, Himself the knower of rasa, sat at ease with Gadadhara; and when Rama had retired to rest, longing for the rasa dance and intoxicated with the rasa of delight, He rejoiced in Him who is the delight of the delights of rasa10.

Thus ends the eighteenth sarga, "Beholding Sri Gopinatha after the Journey through Gauda" (Gauda-desha-bhramana-anantaram shri-gopinatha-darshana), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Ramakeli: a village near Gauda, the capital of Bengal, where Sanatana and his younger brother Rupa served as ministers of the sultan.
  2. A straw between the teeth: a sign of utter humility and of begging forgiveness.
  3. The lost holy places of Vraja, which Rupa and Sanatana uncovered at the Lord's command.
  4. Kanai Natyashala (see sarga 17, verses 9–11).
  5. Achyuta (Achyutananda): the son of Advaita Acharya.
  6. The four kinds of food: what is chewed, sucked, licked and drunk.
  7. Gopinatha: the Deity of Krishna with the flute at Puri served by Gadadhara Pandita (Tota-Gopinatha).
  8. According to the Gaudiya Vaishnavas, Gadadhara Pandita is an incarnation of Sri Radha.
  9. In verses 26–27 the subject is not clearly expressed; the translation is conjectural.
  10. The second half of the verse survives only in the Bengali edition (Calcutta, 1945) and plays on the words rasa (the dance), rasa (the taste of love) and Rama; the translation is conjectural. Rama is Nityananda. The rasa here is spiritual: Gauranga, Krishna Himself, tastes the love of Radha manifest in Gadadhara (v. 25; cf. 2.03, note to v. 17) — pure prema without a shadow of the mundane.
